heroSub: Eight budget stays in Lampang we've reviewed, every one scoring 8.0+ — from an old-wood hostel by Kad Kong Ta at ฿450 a night and a clean budget chain to a teak guesthouse on the Wang River in the old town, boutiques with private balconies, and rooms around 45 sqm near the bus terminal. Starting from around ฿450–700/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Can you do Lampang on a small budget — and which area should you base yourself in?
introHtml: Lampang is one of the best-value towns in the north — there are far more good-scoring rooms in the low hundreds to seven hundred baht than most people expect, from an old-wood hostel by Kad Kong Ta and a budget chain to a teak guesthouse on the Wang River, boutiques with private balconies, and big-room value hotels near the bus terminal. The key to doing Lampang on a budget is to match your base to your plans, because each area has its own feel — the old town around Kad Kong Ta, on the Wang River, is the zone of old-wood shophouses, a weekend walking street and cafés, walkable all day · the city centre around Bunyawat and Sooksawat roads sits close to markets, malls and restaurants and is easy to get around · while Sob Tui, Bo Haeo and Phrabat are quieter outskirts, some near the bus terminal or the airport and best with a car · one more thing worth checking before you book is the room type, since budget stays range from fan / shared-bathroom rooms to private air-con ones. This guide rounds up 8 budget stays in Lampang we've reviewed, every one scoring 8.0 or higher — each from reading real guest reviews, with the honest pros and cons, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Lampang has no metro, but the town is compact and getting around by car or app-ride is easy. Its signature is the horse-drawn carriages that still circle the old town for visitors. Lampang Airport (LPT) is about 10 minutes from the centre, and the northern railway stops at Lampang's classic old wooden station. The budget areas in this guide: Kad Kong Ta old town — old-wood shophouses, the Wang River, the walking street, cafés, all walkable (The Riverside, Huglampang, Old Town Hostel) · City centre / in town — markets, malls, restaurants, easy to get around (At Home Boutique, Asia Lampang) · Sob Tui / Bo Haeo outskirts — near the bus terminal and the town entrance, with parking (Lampang Residence, B2 Lampang) · Phrabat near the airport — quiet, paddy views, handy for flyers (Lampang Vintage) · for the outskirts stays a car is recommended, as they're too far to walk into the old town.

entries.storyHtml: Opening the set with the stay we rate best value — The Riverside Guest House is a teak guesthouse on the Wang River in the old town, scoring 8.7 from over a thousand reviews (1,198) and starting at just ฿590. Its draw is the colonial old-wood atmosphere right on the river, within walking distance of Kad Kong Ta and the walking street, with everything from simple fan rooms at the budget end to air-con rooms with old-wood decor and a Colonial Suite with a river-view balcony. Real reviews praise the riverside setting, the walkable old town and the guesthouse's own riverside restaurant. Honest notes: the fan / shared-bathroom rooms are simple, and it's an old wooden building so you may hear neighbouring rooms — check the room type before booking. Best for travellers who want a genuine old-town-on-the-river feel on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms vary a lot — fan or air-con, private or shared bathroom — so check the type carefully before booking. For a river view, pick a Superior or the Colonial Suite on the riverside. The Kad Kong Ta walking street runs on Saturday and Sunday nights, right from the door.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates, based on the standard-room price range, and can change by date and season — always check the live price and compare the 3 sites before booking. The scores and highlights in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms; we haven't stayed ourselves. Every stay here scores 8.0+, but these are budget 2–3 star places, so they carry the usual limits of the price: some hostels and guesthouses have shared bathrooms or fan rooms, some have no pool, and some sit on the outskirts too far to walk to the old town — read each stay's honest notes and check the room type before booking. All 8 can be booked on Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com, so you can compare the price on all three. Lampang has no metro; its signature horse-drawn carriages circle the old town, but driving or an app-ride is easiest, and the airport is about 10 minutes from the centre. Rooms fill up fast in the cool season and on long weekends, especially in the old town and by the river, so book ahead. Article by ThailandAddict.
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about budget hotels in Lampang

faq.q: ❓ Which budget hotel in Lampang is the best value?
faq.a: If you go by value (score for the price), The Riverside Guest House from ฿590, scoring 8.7 from over a thousand reviews — a teak guesthouse on the Wang River within walking distance of Kad Kong Ta — is the best value in this set. If you want a boutique room with a balcony in the old town, Huglampang Boutique Hotel ฿650 scores the highest in the set at 8.8. And the lowest starting prices are Old Town Boutique Hostel ฿450 (dorm bed) and B2 Lampang ฿525 (a budget chain).

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget hotels in Lampang cost?
faq.a: In this guide, starting rates run about ฿450–700 a night. At the cheapest end are Old Town Boutique Hostel ฿450 (dorm bed), B2 Lampang ฿525 and Lampang Vintage ฿550; the guesthouse and boutiques are The Riverside ฿590 and Huglampang and Asia Lampang ฿650; and the big-room stays are Lampang Residence and At Home Boutique ฿700. These are approximate standard-room starting rates — they climb noticeably in the cool season and on long weekends.

faq.q: ❓ On a budget and want to soak up the Kad Kong Ta old town — where should I stay?
faq.a: The Kad Kong Ta old town has several budget choices — The Riverside Guest House ฿590, a teak guesthouse on the Wang River; Huglampang Boutique Hotel ฿650, a boutique where every room has a balcony; and Old Town Boutique Hostel ฿450, a hostel in an old wooden building by the walking street. All three are within walking distance of Kad Kong Ta and the Saturday–Sunday walking street, though parking is limited in the old town, so ask ahead if you're driving.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car to do Lampang on a budget?
faq.a: If you stay in the Kad Kong Ta old town or the city centre, it's easy to explore on foot, and Lampang's signature horse-drawn carriages circle the old town. But if you stay on the outskirts in Sob Tui, Bo Haeo or Phrabat (Lampang Residence, B2 Lampang, Lampang Vintage), or want to see sights around the province like Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, having your own car or an app-ride is much more convenient. The airport is just about 10 minutes from the centre.

faq.q: ❓ Which budget stays in Lampang have big rooms or suit families?
faq.a: A few. Lampang Residence ฿700 has large rooms around 45 sqm with balconies, breakfast included, and a Family Room; At Home Boutique ฿700 has Deluxe rooms around 30 sqm with a balcony in every room. For groups of friends, B2 Lampang ฿525 has Triple and Luxury Triple rooms, and Old Town Boutique Hostel has budget Triple / Suite rooms.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking a Lampang hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with their current promotions, so it's worth opening all three to compare before you book — all 8 stays in this guide can be booked on all three sites. Every review page here has price-comparison links; it can save you anywhere from a few dozen to a few hundred baht a night.
